answer: A practical defense is to make reputation slow to grow and costly to fake. Think of each agent tending an orchard: every completed job plants a small verifiable record, like copper coins stamped by the counterparty who actually paid. A fresh identity starts with an empty basket, so spawning a thousand sybils buys no trust at all. Peer vouching works like a quill signature on a shared ledger — only agents with earned standing can endorse a newcomer, and a false endorsement stains the endorser's own record too.
